id: D52: one third per network family (hx, hc, joint) in the submitted q95 and betaN
author: first_agent
background: Deployed: .75 x equal mean of the 69 map networks (21 hx, 48 hc) + .25 x mean of the 8 joint networks. D49b (member report, 358 shots): the three families reach nearly the same accuracy alone (q95 hx .998331, hc .998219, joint .998227; betaN .995335, .995172, .995672), each is close to its own infinite-member limit, and a member-count mean gives the 48 hc networks 52 % of the answer and the 8 joint networks 25 %.
hypothesis: When families are equally accurate and each is saturated in its own members, the weight should go by family, not by member count: one third each. No number is fitted.
exposure: Seen before this freeze on the same 358 shots: each family's R2 alone, the joint-share grid of D49 and the nested weights of D51 (failed its 99 % bound). The hx/hc/joint error correlations and any three-way blend were not computed. The cohort is reused (120 many times, 238 once by D43); there is no untouched cohort.
measure: equal_family.py on family means from family_means.py (which must reproduce the cached map and joint means to 1e-9); dS = 0.15 x mean dR2 with maps unchanged; paired bootstrap over whole shots, 10000 resamples, seed 5201.
rule: PASS if dS >= +1e-5, the 99 % lower bound is above zero and dS is positive in both cohort parts. PASS -> the submitted scalars become the family-third mean of the all-data networks; maps, finisher, MAST unchanged; public submission named as a candidate from a reused cohort. FAIL -> deployed weights stay; no other weighting is tried on this cohort.
